scenes.text: Their webs stretch for metres through the trees. Some colonies hold tens of thousands of spiders.
When a moth or grasshopper hits the silk, hundreds rush in together. Then they all freeze. Then they all move again.
A 2022 study found they stop and start in sync so the prey's struggling vibrations aren't drowned out by their own footsteps.
That's how a quarter-inch spider brings down prey hundreds of times its size.

description:
Thousands of spiders share one web, and they hunt as one.
Anelosimus eximius is a social spider from the rainforests of Central and South America. Each spider is about a quarter inch long, but their shared webs stretch for metres and some colonies are reported to hold tens of thousands of individuals. A 2022 study in PNAS from the University of Toulouse showed that when prey lands, the spiders advance and freeze in synchrony, pausing so the prey's vibrations can be heard over their own footsteps. Working together they take moths and grasshoppers hundreds of times their size.
Would you walk under a web the size of a small house?
first_comment: There is no leader. The whole colony coordinates through vibrations in the silk alone. What other animals hunt in a pack with no boss?
